correctness.rationale: The cyclic XOR obstruction and forest two-complement solution lemma establish the exact test for all n,k. Counting uses Cayley and labeled set partitions. The upper 2r bound uses balanced vertex assignments per component and shore-complement symmetry; star construction attains it when n>=3r+1. Small-forest theorem follows from maximum subset-sum gap <= maximum term and enough isolated vertices. Independent exhaustive comparisons (168146 across n<=6) and coefficient checks agree, but infinite claims are proven separately.

value.rationale: An exact complete classification of shattered supports for natural globally constrained cuts yields the entire polynomial of feasible query supports via integer partitions. The dimension bound is sharp for every cardinality k in a large-n range, while the uniform forest lemma explains robust realizability of arbitrary binary edge assignments. The result does not claim an efficient polynomial-time enumeration or all-n scalar dimension formula.
